title: Purification of hetero-oligomeric protein variants using a modified tandem affinity purification approach
protocol: Reconstitute recombinant protein constructs in bacterial cells such as E. coli BL21 (DE3) or Rosetta (DE3) pLysS strains.
Pick single isolated colonies of the transformed cells and grow them ∼16–18 hours in LB broth containing the appropriate antibiotic at 37°C.
Isolate plasmids from the cultured cells using miniprep method according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Inoculate about 1–2% (v/v) of the grown primary culture into each liter of LB broth containing the appropriate antibiotic.
Grow cells further at 37°C (180 rpm) until the optical density at 600 nm reaches ∼0.6 AU.
Add IPTG to a final concentration of 0.3 mM to induce protein expression once the required OD is achieved.
Incubate the cultured cells with induced IPTG at 18°C for 18 hours at 180 rpm.
Collect 10 μL samples of the pre- and post-induction cultures for analysis by SDS-PAGE.
Harvest induced cells for protein production by centrifuging at 4°C using Beckman Coulter centrifuge (Rotor ID JA-10) or equivalent for 30–45 min at ∼3000 × g.
Store harvested cells at −80°C until protein purification.
Resuspend the cell pellet in lysis buffer (Ni-NTA lysis buffer/ MBP protein purification lysis buffer) using a glass rod or by gentle vortexing, with intermittent incubation on ice.
Transfer solubilization mixture to a pre-chilled sonicator tube and sonicate homogeneous suspension for 1 min on, 2 min off, amplitude of 50%, for 5–6 cycles.
Centrifuge the sonicated mixture at ∼17,000–31,000 × g for 50–60 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant carefully to a clean, chilled 50-mL Falcon tube without disturbing the pellet.
Prepare a sample of the supernatant and a sample from the pellet for analysis by SDS-PAGE.
Filter the supernatant using a sterile 0.45 μm syringe filter.
Transfer the filtered supernatant in a clean pre-chilled falcon tube.
Pre-chill all buffers used for protein purification at 4°C before starting the process.
Load filtrate onto Ni-NTA agarose resin for histidine-tagged proteins or amylose resin for MBP-tagged proteins in a glass/plastic column.
Place the purification column on a rocker and gently mix at constant slow speed for 45–60 min at 4°C to promote protein binding.
Allow resin beads to settle after incubation, then collect flow-through containing non-specific cellular proteins.
Prepare a small volume of sample (∼20 μL) for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Save the flow-through until the analysis at 4°C is done.
Wash the column with the equilibration buffer until the coloration in Bradford’s test becomes negligible.
Increase the concentration of imidazole or maltose in the elution buffer in a stepwise manner.
For Ni-NTA resin purification, wash with ∼30 mL of 10 mM, 50 mM, 100 mM, and 250 mM imidazole-containing elution buffer.
For MBP-tagged protein purification, wash with ∼30 mL of 10 mM and 20 mM maltose-containing elution buffer.
His-tag proteins generally elute in 250–300 mM imidazole-containing buffer.
MBP-tagged proteins elute in 10 mM maltose-containing elution buffer.
Pull together elution fractions of the purified protein variant.
Add recommended units of TEV protease in a protease to target protein ratio as recommended by the manufacturer or standardized for laboratory-purified TEV protease.
Incubate the mixture for 12–18 h at 4°C–22°C, depending on the activity previously determined for the TEV protease.
Incubate a small aliquot of the uncleaved target protein at similar conditions as a negative control for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Prepare 20 μL samples (control and test) for SDS-PAGE analysis to determine successful cleavage of the affinity tag from the target protein.
Increase the amount of TEV protease if uncleaved protein is visible in the SDS-PAGE sample.
Load the cleaved protein onto an appropriate resin after SDS-PAGE analysis.
Incubate the MBP cleaved protein fraction onto Ni-NTA resin.
Repeat steps 13–19 for purification as suggested.
Wash with gradient buffers as mentioned in steps 15–16 for Ni-NTA purification.
Standardize the volume of gradient buffer used in each washing step based on impurity levels.
Elute the target protein using an elution buffer containing 50 mM imidazole.
Save the flow-through and each elution fraction at 4°C until analysis.
Take 10 μL samples during each step of gradient wash and elution for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Extensively rinse the membrane of protein concentrators with autoclaved deionized water.
Equilibrate the membrane in equilibration buffer for 16-18 hours at 4°C.
Concentrate purified elution fractions using an Amicon tangential-flow spin filter or stirred cell concentrator.
Pool the eluted pure fractions for a particular protein obtained from the affinity chromatography purification.
Load the pooled fractions onto the equilibrated membrane concentrator.
Concentrate the sample at 4°C until the desired concentration and volume is reached.
Discard the filtrate at each regular interval to maintain the reservoir load on the concentrator membrane.
Run the concentrated sample on SDS-PAGE to determine the purity of the protein.
Identify any impurities present in the SDS-PAGE results.
If impurities are identified, run the concentrated sample through a size-exclusion column.
Separate and isolate the pure protein fraction from the column.
Estimate the concentration of the final protein sample using Bradford measurements or by measuring absorption at 280 nm.
Perform thermal and/or chemical denaturation studies using fluorescence spectroscopy, circular dichroism spectroscopy, or nano-DSF to assess the stability of individual parent homomers.
Check if both homomer variants have melting temperatures within a suitable range.
If stable temperatures are confirmed, perform heat denaturation of the reconstituted mixture at a temperature that is lower than the lowest melting point.
If proteins are less thermostable, opt for chemical denaturation using reagents such as guanidium hydrochloride and urea.
Perform folding studies of each parent homomer at different concentrations of chemical denaturant using circular dichroism spectroscopy.
Mix 500–1000 μL of each concentrated parent homomeric protein variant in equimolar concentrations (50–60 μM).
Dilute the reconstituted mixture up to a 15-fold dilution in an equilibration buffer containing 6 M guanidinium chloride (pH 8.0).
Incubate the mixture at 50°C for 1-2 hours under slow rocking conditions.
Transfer the denatured protein mixture to a dialysis apparatus with an appropriate molecular-weight cut-off (10 kDa).
Seal the dialysis apparatus at both ends and place it in a beaker containing 1 L–3 L of renaturation buffer pre-chilled at 4°C.
Incubate this assembly under constant gentle stirring for 3-4 hours at 4°C.
Replace half the volume of the used dialysate renaturation buffer with fresh renaturation buffer containing 10% glycerol.
Incubate under constant gentle stirring conditions for 3-4 hours at 4°C.
Replace the equilibrated renaturation buffer entirely with fresh renaturation buffer containing 10% glycerol and continue the incubation for 3–4 h at 4°C.
Gradually decrease the glycerol content in the renaturation buffer until reaching 5% glycerol, repeating steps as necessary.
Perform two-step dialysis with a fresh buffer A containing only 5% glycerol to remove arginine from the reconstituted protein mixture.
Incubate at 4°C for 3–4 h after each step of dialysis.
Transfer the renatured protein mixture from the dialysis apparatus to pre-chilled falcon tubes carefully.
Filter the solution using a sterile 0.22 μm syringe filter to remove any aggregated protein or particulate matter formed during dialysis.
Load the filtrate onto fresh pre-equilibrated membrane concentrator and concentrate the renatured protein mixture back to the original volume used before diluting with the denaturant.
Transfer the concentrated sample to a clean micro-centrifuge tube.
Spin the tube for 10 min at approximately 13,500 × g and 4°C.
Carefully separate the supernatant.
Store the supernatant in a fresh micro-centrifuge tube at 4°C until further use.
Prepare 20 μL samples of the concentrated renatured mixture for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Prepare 20 μL samples of the concentrated renatured mixture for Native PAGE analysis.
Determine the purity of the total renatured mixture using SDS-PAGE analysis.
Identify any degradation that may have occurred during the denaturation-renaturation process through SDS-PAGE.
Estimate the success of the renaturation process via Native PAGE analysis.
Calculate the percentage of Native PAGE gel to be prepared based on the native molecular weight of each variant ensemble present in the renatured mixture.
Run two sets of identical Native PAGE gels at a constant voltage of 50 V for 5 hours at 4°C.
Use one gel for Coomassie staining.
Set aside the other unstained Native PAGE gel for western blot analysis.
Load the concentrated renatured protein mixture onto fresh Ni-NTA resin pre-equilibrated with buffer A.
Incubate the loaded resin at 4°C.
Centrifuge the tube at 5000–6000 × g for 1 minute to settle the resin beads.
Collect the flow-through carefully.
Prepare a small volume (∼20 μL) of sample for SDS-PAGE analysis to estimate unbound target protein or degraded proteins.
Save the flow-through at 4°C until SDS-PAGE analysis.
Wash the column with equilibration buffer until coloration in Bradford’s test becomes negligible or the 280 nm signal for eluant is near baseline.
Increase imidazole concentration in elution buffer stepwise to elute bound target protein variants.
Use a shallow gradient of imidazole (10–250 mM, with 10 mM intervals) to separate protein variants based on histidine residues.
Incubate about 200 μL of each buffer gradient to avoid unnecessary dilution of the variants.
Elute impurities in the flow-through fraction up to 30 mM imidazole buffer washes.
Elute the first homomeric parent protein with the lowest number of histidine residues between 40–50 mM imidazole buffer washes.
Perform elution step for each gradient under cold conditions by placing collection tubes on ice.
Elute hetero-oligomers between 50–200 mM imidazole buffer washes.
Collect the second homomeric parent protein eluted with the highest number of histidine residues in imidazole.
Micro-centrifuge beads at ∼5000–6000 × g to elute proteins.
Carefully collect and store each fraction immediately at 4°C.
Collect ∼20 μL sample of every elution gradient wash for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Run native PAGE gels in a set of two – use one gel for Coomassie staining, set aside one unstained gel for western blot analysis to confirm purity.
Store fractions containing a single protein variant (>95% pure) at 4°C or flash freeze and store at -80°C.

Transfer the gel slice containing separated protein bands from the unstained native PAGE gel onto a nitrocellulose membrane using Invitrogen wet transfer mini blot module and 1X transfer buffer at 15 V for 60–90 min.
Remove the membrane after transfer is complete.
Block the membrane with 5% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 1X TBST buffer for 1 h.
Stain the gel with Coomassie Blue to check transfer efficiency.
Wash the membrane three to six times with 1X TBST buffer for 5–10 min each after blocking.
Probe protein bands in the blot using primary antibody against the tag present at the C-terminal or N-terminal end of the variant.
Incubate the membrane ∼16–18 h with the recommended/standardized dilution of the primary antibody (e.g., 1:2000 for anti-FLAG antibody) under constant rocking conditions at 4°C.
Remove the membrane from the antibody solution.
Wash the membrane three to six times with 1X TBST buffer for 5–10 min intervals each.
Incubate the membrane at approximately 22°C–24°C for 1 h with a secondary antibody diluted 1:5000 in 1X TBST containing 1% BSA.
Wash the membrane three to six times with 1X TBST buffer for 5–10 min intervals each.
Store the membrane in 1X TBST buffer at 4°C until probing the blot.
Develop the blot using an enhanced chemiluminescence kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
